parts.latex:
An electricity company charges customers 37 cents per kWh for electricity used, $U$, and pays customers 5 cents per kWh for electricity produced, $P$.

The electricity company also charges customers a fee of 71 cents per day.

Which formula should be used to calculate a customer's daily cost of electricity, $C$, in cents?

solutions.latex:
The customer pays a fixed fee of 71 cents, pays $37U$ cents for electricity used, and is paid $5P$ cents for electricity produced.

Payments add to the cost and the payment received is subtracted.
$$C = 71 + 37U - 5P$$
Hence the correct option is A.

meta.self_check: Checked sign of each term against the wording.

6137.stem: Sienna has moved into a four-bedroom unit which she will share with three friends. She is responsible for one quarter of the rent and one quarter of the utilities (electricity and water) for the unit. She has just got her first full time job, which pays \$1964 per fortnight after tax.

parts.latex:
With her new full time job paying \$1964 per fortnight after tax, she needs to budget for these expenses. The rent on the unit is \$492 per week and the most recent quarterly bills for electricity and water were \$572 and \$260 respectively.

To safeguard against potential increases Sienna budgets an additional 20\% of these expenses.

How much should she budget from her fortnightly pay to cover her share of these expenses?

She is also purchasing a car using a loan which has monthly payments of \$572. The car has weekly running expenses of \$48 and annual service, insurance, and registration expenses of \$ 1831.70. How much should she budget from her fortnightly pay to cover her car related expenses?

Sienna pays \$145 per week toward household groceries and food and allows \$40 per day to buy lunch and other incidental daily expenses.

How much does she have left from her fortnightly pay to save for other major purchases and entertainment?

solutions.latex:
Sienna pays one quarter of the rent. Rent is weekly, so a fortnight is 2 weeks.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Share of rent} &= \dfrac{492}{4} \times 2 \\ &= \$246 \end{aligned}$$
Bills are quarterly, so there are 4 sets of bills a year and 26 fortnights.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Yearly utility bills} &= 4 \times (572 + 260) \\ &= \$3328 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Her share of bills} &= (3328 \div 26) \div 4 \\ &= \$32 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Current accommodation expenses} &= 246 + 32 \\ &= \$278 \end{aligned}$$
Add 20% for possible increases.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Budget} &= 1.2 \times 278 \\ &= \$333.60 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Makes progress towards current accommodation expenses, or equivalent merit
Finds share of utility bills, or equivalent merit

meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

solutions.latex:
Monthly payments are 12 a year and there are 26 fortnights in a year.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Fortnightly loan payment} &= 572 \times \dfrac{12}{26} \\ &= \$264 \end{aligned}$$
Running costs are weekly, so double them.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Running costs} &= 48 \times 2 \\ &= \$96 \end{aligned}$$
Annual expenses are divided by 26.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Fortnightly bills} &= 1831.70 \div 26 \\ &\approx \$70.45 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total car budget} &= 264 + 96 + 70.45 \\ &= \$430.45 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: At least 2 correct fortnightly amounts, or equivalent merit

meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

solutions.latex:
Groceries are weekly, so double them. Lunch is daily, so multiply by 14 days.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Fortnightly food and groceries} &= 145 \times 2 \\ &= \$290 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Fortnightly lunch and incidentals} &= 40 \times 14 \\ &= \$560 \end{aligned}$$
Using the results of parts (a) and (b):
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total budget} &= 333.60 + 430.45 + 290 + 560 \\ &= \$1614.05 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Savings} &= 1964 - 1614.05 \\ &= \$349.95 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Works out total budget, or equivalent merit

6291.stem:
Alyssa has a net weekly income of \$1180 per week. She has created a weekly budget to help manage her money.

\exfigure{718_q7_1}

parts.latex: Find the value of $\mathbf{X}$, the amount that Alyssa allocates towards electricity each week.

Alyssa's electricity provider has recently increased the price of electricity. For the last three weeks, she put aside her savings as well as her electricity money to pay the bill.

How much money has she put aside altogether to pay the bill?

Her electricity bill is \$1240. It is due in two weeks time. Alyssa realises she has not put aside enough money to pay this bill.

How could Alyssa reallocate non-essential funds in her budget, so she has enough money to pay the bill? Justify your answer with suitable reasons and calculations.

solutions.latex:
The weekly allocations must total the net income.

$$\begin{aligned} X &= 1180-(350+90+20+30+180+50+60+140+100+80) \\ &= \$80 \end{aligned}$$

meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

Each week she puts aside $\$80$ for electricity plus $\$80$ for savings, for $3$ weeks.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total} &= (\$80+\$80)\times 3 \\ &= \$480 \end{aligned}$$

parts.latex:
Sophia is planning to take a holiday a year from now, and there are four options that she is considering.

\extable{308_q12_t1}

She earns \$1 240.00 per week after deductions.

She has calculated her weekly spending to be \$750.00 and she needs to put \$1 540 away each month to cover major bills.

If she saves the rest of her income toward her holiday, which is the most expensive holiday that she could afford to take?

solutions.latex:
Weekly savings:
$$\begin{aligned} 1240 - 750 &= \$490 \end{aligned}$$
Over one year (52 weeks):
$$\begin{aligned} 490 \times 52 &= \$25\,480 \end{aligned}$$
Major bills over the year:
$$\begin{aligned} 1540 \times 12 &= \$18\,480 \end{aligned}$$
Amount available for the holiday:
$$\begin{aligned} 25\,480 - 18\,480 &= \$7000 \end{aligned}$$
The most expensive holiday costing no more than $\$7000$ is the Kimberley Adventure ($\$6400$). The Grand Tour of Asia ($\$10\,400$) is too expensive.

The cost of gas is determined using the table below:

parts.latex: Maria used 7000MJ of gas in this period. What is the charge?
Maria has decided to reduce her energy bills. She has a target of \$200 for gas. What is the maximum number of MJ she is allowed in this period? Answer correct to the nearest megajoule.

solutions.latex:
The first $3000$ MJ is charged at \$0.05280 per MJ and the next $4000$ MJ at \$0.04620 per MJ.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Charge} &= 3000\times 0.05280+4000\times 0.04620 \\ &= \$343.20 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Calculates one tier correctly, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The first $3000$ MJ costs
$$3000\times 0.05280=\$158.40$$
Let $x$ be the extra MJ at \$0.04620.
$$\begin{aligned} 158.40+0.04620x &= 200 \\ x &= \dfrac{41.60}{0.04620} \\ &\approx 900 \text{ MJ} \end{aligned}$$
$$\text{Maximum usage}=3000+900=3900 \text{ MJ}$$
criteria: Sets up and solves for the extra usage, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
An energy company charges for gas usage over a three-month period according to the table.

\extable{288_q33_t1}

Hannah is trying to budget her household bills. She has a maximum of \$150 set aside for her gas bill.

What is the maximum amount of gas, in megajoules, that Hannah can use in the three-month period? Give your answer correct to the nearest whole number.

solutions.latex:
Cost of $3000$ MJ:
$$3000\times0.0892=\$267.60$$
This is more than $\$150$, so find the amount of gas for $\$150$.
$$\begin{aligned}x\times0.0892&=150\\ x&=\dfrac{150}{0.0892}\\ &=1681.6144\ldots\\ &\approx1681\text{ MJ}\end{aligned}$$
Round down: $1682$ MJ would give a bill greater than $\$150$.
$$\therefore\ \text{maximum} = 1681\text{ MJ}$$
criteria: Attempts to find the cost of $3000$ MJ, or equivalent merit

Answer unchanged (1681 MJ).

7487.stem:
Angus lives at home and pays board to his parents. He has a car to pay off and maintain. Angus earns \$650 per week after tax. His budget is shown below.

\extable{712_q7_t1}

parts.latex: Calculate Angus’ annual after-tax income. Assume there are exactly 52 weeks in a year.
Calculate the total of Angus’ current annual expenditure.
How much, on average, is Angus able to save per week?

solutions.latex:
There are 52 weeks in a year, so
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Annual income} &= 650\times 52 \\ &= \$33\,800 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Annual after-tax income} = \$33\,800$$

meta.generated_note: Written by us; source had no solution.
meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

solutions.latex:
Convert every expense to a yearly amount (52 weeks or 26 fortnights in a year).
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Board} &= 85\times 52 = \$4420 \\ \text{Car maintenance} &= \$938 \\ \text{Registration and insurance} &= \$1252 \\ \text{Car repayments} &= 249\times 26 = \$6474 \\ \text{Clothing} &= 60\times 26 = \$1560 \\ \text{Entertainment} &= 68\times 52 = \$3536 \\ \text{Fuel} &= 73\times 52 = \$3796 \\ \text{Gym} &= 30\times 26 = \$780 \\ \text{Health insurance} &= \$2159 \end{aligned}$$
Adding these,
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total} &= 4420+938+1252+6474+1560+3536+3796+780+2159 \\ &= \$24\,915 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Total annual expenditure} = \$24\,915$$
criteria: Converts expenses to annual amounts correctly for most items, or equivalent merit

meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

solutions.latex:
Annual savings are income less expenditure.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Annual savings} &= 33\,800-24\,915 \\ &= \$8885 \end{aligned}$$
Divide by 52 weeks.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Weekly savings} &= \dfrac{8885}{52} \\ &\approx \$170.87 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Angus saves about } \$170.87 \text{ per week}$$

meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

Charlie has a sporting injury and finds his medical expenses increase to \$65.00 per week.

Suggest how he can reduce areas of discretionary spending to prevent his budget having a weekly loss. At least two areas to be listed.

solutions.latex:

$$65-28=\$37 \text{ more per week, and } 37-19=\$18$$
He could reduce spending on entertainment, cash incidentals and personal items.

parts.latex:
A section of the electricity bill for Corie's share-house is shown below.

\exfigure{708_q34_1}

There are five people living in the house who share the electricity costs equally

If she pays the account on 2nd September, how much would she need to collect from each of her housemates?

solutions.latex:
Paying on 2nd September earns the discount.
$$\text{Discount} = \$64.33$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Amount payable} &= \$643.26 - \$64.33 \\ &= \$578.93 \end{aligned}$$
Share equally among five people:
$$\begin{aligned} 578.93 \div 5 &= \$115.79 \\ &\approx \$115.80 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \$115.80 \text{ each}$$
criteria: Finds the amount payable after discount, or equivalent merit
